title: Keep a legacy Windows VM password with $$ working after the Quattro migration
head: dfb360c7b1e7
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A legacy YAML-escaped backslash plus $$ is decoded as raw text, not the password the guest has
leads.consequence: For PASSWORD: "legacy\\$$pass", Compose YAML resolves the pair of backslashes to one, then $$ to $, so the guest has legacy\$pass. Migration stores legacy\\$pass in the RDP credential and re-escapes that different string into the root compose. The user cannot log into the existing guest with the migrated RDP password (and the rewritten Compose password also differs). The existing new fixture lacks YAML escapes.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; YAML escapes not decoded; Opus reproduced (opus/reproducers/yaml-escapes.md). Published as the finding.

leads.summary: Combining #8662 with this PR preserves a raw $$ legacy USERNAME as RDP identity
leads.consequence: For an old Compose USERNAME: "legacy$$user", Compose supplied legacy$user to a guest that accepts a dollar in local account names. This PR decodes only PASSWORD. Today the writer rejects the raw username and migration fails; #8662 instead lets migration complete by writing docker to the new Compose but saves legacy$$user for RDP, so the connection cannot authenticate to the original local account. Decode the separately preserved RDP username before storing it, coordinate this with #8662 rather than decoding the writer username into an invalid format.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; Opus source-level; published in Details as source reading only.

Preserve the decoder while resolving TZ/REGION. GitHub reports #8228 MERGEABLE against quattro individually; that is not a test of their joint merge.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; Textual conflict; published in Details.

leads.summary: New migration test confirms the shell writer's own inverse, not Docker Compose parsing
leads.consequence: The new assertions correctly catch a missing $$-to-$ substitution on the simple fixture: the new fixture paired with base helper exits 1. They also pass on the head while a valid YAML-escaped backslash immediately before $$ yields a wrong private credential, as H1 demonstrates. Extend the fixture to include a decoded YAML escape and assert the real guest-side Compose value or a validated Compose parser result instead of only invoking helper unescape; this is a lower-priority coverage issue separate from the behaviour.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; Not published; covered by F1 reproducer.

leads.summary: A mixed escaped dollar and subsequent Compose variable remains unresolved
leads.consequence: Conditional on a legacy value such as PASSWORD: "p$$$WORD" and WORD unset when its guest was configured: Compose would supply p$, while this substitution turns the raw string into p$$WORD and the new writer preserves both dollars literally. With WORD set during the legacy bring-up the guest password differs again. Recovering the historical interpolation environment is not generally possible, so detect and ask for the actual guest password rather than claiming every $$-containing value is safely migrated. This affects only mixed $$/$NAME cases; pure $$ and lone $ still work.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; PR declares $name cases out of scope; not published.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** A legacy password containing `\\` or `\"` still migrates to a value the guest never had.

### YAML escapes in the legacy password are not decoded

Compose parses the legacy value as a YAML double-quoted string before it interpolates `$$`, so `PASSWORD: "legacy\\pa\"ss$$1"` reached the guest as `legacy\pa"ss$1`. The new line undoes only the `$$` layer, so the RDP credential holds, and the rewritten compose delivers, `legacy\\pa\"ss$1`. **Impact:** RDP login fails after migration for such passwords; this predates the PR and needs a typed `\\` or `\"`, so it is likely rare.

**Suggested change:** Use the existing helper, `password=$(unescape "$password")`, which gives the same result as this PR on every `$` case tested and also reverses `\\` and `\"`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at dfb360c)</summary>

Output below is verbatim except that the random test scratch directory is shown as `<scratch>`.

Reviewed head: `dfb360c7b1e7d8624f67b4406cf12da3340bb39e`.

## What Docker Compose gave the guest

A 3.x (or 4.0.0) install wrote the typed password verbatim between the quotes, and Compose parses that YAML double-quoted scalar before it interpolates. A legacy line `PASSWORD: "legacy\\pa\"ss$$1"` therefore reached the container as `legacy\pa"ss$1`.

Actual output, Docker Compose 5.5.1, `docker-compose -f docker-compose.yml config --format json` on:

```yaml
services:
  windows:
    image: dockurr/windows
    environment:
      PASSWORD: "legacy\\pa\"ss$$1"
```

The PASSWORD field of the JSON output, printed after JSON decoding:

```
legacy\pa"ss$$1
```

`config` doubles every `$` in its output (`bytes.ReplaceAll(content, "$", "$$")` in docker/compose `cmd/compose/config.go`), so the value Compose passes to the container is `legacy\pa"ss$1`.

## Test case (PR's own test style)

Append to the end of `test/shell.d/windows-vm-compose-test.sh`:

```bash

# Docker Compose reads the legacy value through YAML first: "legacy\\pa\"ss$$1"
# reached the guest as legacy\pa"ss$1, so migration must store that password.
reset_case
mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/windows"
cat >"$LEGACY_COMPOSE_FILE" <<'LEG'
services:
  windows:
    environment:
      RAM_SIZE: "16G"
      CPU_CORES: "6"
      DISK_SIZE: "128G"
      USERNAME: "legacyuser"
      PASSWORD: "legacy\\pa\"ss$$1"
      TZ: "America/New_York"
LEG
migrate_legacy_compose
[[ $(read_credential PASSWORD) == 'legacy\pa"ss$1' ]] || fail "migration kept the legacy YAML escaping in the RDP password" "got: $(read_credential PASSWORD)"
[[ $(unescape "$(read_compose_value PASSWORD "$COMPOSE")") == 'legacy\pa"ss$1' ]] || fail "migration changed the guest password"
pass "migration decodes the legacy YAML escapes as well as \$\$"
```

Run: `bash test/shell.d/windows-vm-compose-test.sh`

## Actual output at the reviewed head (exit 1)

Last lines of stdout:

```
ok - credentials are atomically replaced as a private regular file
ok - disk-space checks follow the storage symlink target
Migrating Windows VM configuration to <scratch>/win/docker-compose.yml ...
```

stderr:

```
got: legacy\\pa\"ss$1
not ok - migration kept the legacy YAML escaping in the RDP password
```

The `$$` was decoded by the PR, but the YAML escapes `\\` and `\"` were not, so the RDP credential (and the rewritten compose) hold `legacy\\pa\"ss$1` while the guest has `legacy\pa"ss$1`.

## Actual output with the one-line change `password=$(unescape "$password")` in place of `password=${password//\$\$/\$}` (exit 0)

```
ok - credentials are atomically replaced as a private regular file
ok - disk-space checks follow the storage symlink target
Migrating Windows VM configuration to <scratch>/win/docker-compose.yml ...
ok - migration decodes the legacy YAML escapes as well as $$
```

stderr: empty. The same run executes the whole file, including the PR's own `legacy$$pass` assertions, which still pass with `unescape`.

## Scope and limits

- Pre-existing: the merge-base migration also keeps these escapes (it additionally keeps the `$$`). Nothing regresses at the head.
- How often a real legacy password contains `\\` or `\"` is unknown; a lone backslash before most other letters is invalid YAML, so Compose would have refused that compose and the VM would not have been installed.
- `unescape` does not model other YAML escapes (`\t`, `\n`, `\xNN`, ...) or `$name` interpolation; those stay as they are with or without the change.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- **PR description:** its last paragraph expects basecamp/omarchy#4882 to land on `dev`, but that PR was closed without merging on 2026-09-28. Releases v3.1.0 to v4.0.0 wrote the typed password verbatim, so only passwords typed with `$$` (or hand-edited files) are affected. Installs already migrated by v4.0.1 to v4.0.4 keep the undecoded value.
- **Open PRs:** #8228 edits the adjacent `tz` lines in `migrate_legacy_compose` and conflicts textually with this change; a resolution keeps both. With #8662 merged too, a legacy username containing `$$` would reach RDP undecoded (source reading only).
- **Verified:** the `$$` decoding is correct and the new assertions fail without it; runs of `$` not followed by a name decode as Compose does (`a$$$$b` to `a$$b`); lone `$` (`pa$`, `a$!b`) is unchanged; the credential and the rewritten compose carry the same decoded value; `windows-vm-test.sh` and `windows-key-test.sh` still pass.
</details>
